title.en: Problems with two angles of elevation or depression

text.en: When the angle changes as you walk toward a tower, two equations reveal both the height and the distance.

When two angles of elevation are given, draw one figure with two right triangles that share the same height.
Let the height be h. From the nearer point, the distance is h/tan(angle), and from the farther point it is h/tan(other angle).
The difference of the two distances is the distance the observer moved.
Example: angles 30 and 60 degrees, observer moved 20 m. h/tan 30 - h/tan 60 = 20.
So h root 3 - h/root 3 = 20, giving h x 2/root 3 = 20 and h = 10 root 3 m.
For two objects seen from a tower top, use angles of depression and take care with which one is nearer.
Use the same tan ratio each time, and keep root 3 as it is until the last step.
Always check that the answer is reasonable by drawing the triangles to scale.

problem.en: From the top of a 75 m lighthouse, the angles of depression of two ships are 30 and 45 degrees on the same side. Find the distance between ships.

text.en: Nearer ship: 75/tan 45 = 75 m. Farther ship: 75/tan 30 = 75 root 3 m.

prompt.en: How do you set up a two-angle problem?

commonMisconceptions.en: Using the same triangle for both angles

points.en: Two angles give two right triangles with a common height.
Distances are h/tan(angle); their difference equals the walk.
Keep surds exact until the last step.
